title: Ops soft-restart kickoff speech + Q&A + slack templates
content:
Purpose:
Quick notes / speaking track for the weekend "soft restart" kickoff we want leadership to use when joining the ops bridge. This is intentionally short, human, and empathetic — not a technical postmortem. Also includes quick Q&A crib and ready-to-paste Slack blurb templates.

Audience: ops oncall, cross-functional engineers standing by, product leads, customer success observers, and execs who might pop into the bridge.

Topline for an exec (30–45s):
- Thank you — quick acknowledgement: we know some customers saw elevated latency / throttles overnight.
- What we are doing right now: coordinated soft restart and rolling capacity warmup to clear KV/cache pressure and rebalance traffic.
- Why this approach: avoids a hard cut, reduces cold-start errors, aims to restore normal latencies without user-visible failures.
- What to expect in the next 60–90 minutes: staged node restarts (no more than 10% at a time), progressive traffic ramp, continuous health checks; we'll update at regular 15-min beats.
- Call to action for teams: please avoid non-essential deploys and schema changes until we confirm stable metrics; if you own customer escalations, check queued cases and prioritize anything labeled P0/latency.

Tone cues (for speaker):
- Keep it calm and definitive — we have a plan and are executing.
- No blame; focus on mitigation and customer impact.
- Use plain language; avoid implementation detail unless asked.

Short speaking script (copy / paste friendly):
"Hi everyone — quick update. We observed elevated token-latency and connection churn affecting a subset of requests. We’re initiating a controlled soft restart sequence to relieve caching pressure and rebalance capacity. This is a phased restart: small batches of nodes, health checks between phases, and a gradual traffic ramp. Expect intermittent slow responses for a short window while we stabilize. Our priority is to keep user-facing failures low while we bring metrics back to normal. We’ll post cadence updates every 15 minutes and will call for wider coordination if anything changes. Thank you to everyone on the bridge — we’ve got the right people on this."

Key metrics to watch (ops crib):
- p50/p95 token latency by region and model route
- request error rate (5xx + connection errors) per route
- queue length / in-flight request counts per worker
- KV cache hit ratio and STDERR GC/eviction counters
- infra-level metrics: GPU utilization, OOMs, container restarts

Q&A crib (short answers):
Q: How long will this take?
A: Expect measurable stabilization within 30–90 minutes; full normalization may take a few hours depending on compaction and cache warmup.

Q: Will customers see failures?
A: We expect some increased latency; hard failures should be rare because we're doing phased restarts. If a customer is experiencing 5xx spikes, flag them as P0.

Q: Can we roll back or abort the restart?
A: We can pause the sequence between batches. If metrics worsen, we will halt and open an incident review; the rollback path depends on which layer causes regression (runtime vs infra).

Q: Are we changing any config or models?
A: Not during the soft restart unless a rollback for an immediate regression is required. No model swaps during the window.

Slack / internal async templates (paste exactly):
1) Bridge join (short):
"Joining bridge for soft-restart window — phased node restarts underway to relieve cache pressure. Updates every 15m. Please avoid new deploys. POCs: Nikita (SRE), Arjun (Serving), Lina (Platform)."

2) Customer-facing ops note (CS channel):
"We are performing a controlled restart to address intermittent latency spikes. This may cause brief periods of slower responses for affected requests while we rebalance capacity. We’re monitoring closely and expect stabilization in the next 1–2 hours. Please escalate any critical customer reports to the bridge."

3) Post-stabilization closure (paste later):
"Status update: Traffic stable and key latency/error metrics returning to baseline. We completed the soft restart in X phases; monitoring will continue for the next 4 hours. If you see regression, flag in #ops-urgent."

Escalation and handoff notes:
- Primary bridge leads: Nikita (SRE), Arjun (Serving runtime). Secondary: Lina (Platform infra).
- If retail customers show P0 regression -> page oncall + product-owner.
- If we see repeated OOMs/evictions during warmup -> escalate to infra oncall (pager).
- Document every major decision in the incident timeline (Confluence/incidents).

Open questions / followups (notes-to-self):
- Verify whether the cache eviction threshold config was recently tuned on branch release-quant-2; link PR and confirm no rollouts concurrent with window. (TODO: check GitHub PRs and call out any candidate PRs)
- Add a short checklist to run pre-soft-restart (traffic drain check, queued jobs empty, no open deploys).
- Measure how long warmup takes by model family (small, med, large) — we need hard numbers for next runbook.

Logistics / runbook pointers (for bridge):
- Use the soft-restart sequence documented in Confluence: "soft-restart-runbook-v2".
- Update the incident timeline every 15m with a short one-line update (status, actions taken, next step).
- Assign someone to customer comms (CS partner) and someone to observability notes (trace links, dashboard snapshots).

Reminders for the exec join:
- One-line ask: "Please avoid public comments — we’ll put a clear CS-facing blurb out once we confirm stabilization."
- If asked about root cause: pause — we don't have full RCA; say "root cause under investigation, we will share details after stabilization and initial triage."

Draft short email to execs (for record / optional):
Subject: Weekend soft-restart (latency spike) — short update
Body: We observed transient latency spikes affecting a subset of requests; initiating a controlled soft restart to rebalance capacity and relieve cache pressure. Expect stabilization within 1–2 hours; updates every 15 minutes. No customer-facing statement until we confirm stabilization. Primary leads: Nikita Rao (SRE), Arjun Mehta (Serving).

Notes on wording: keep "soft restart" phrase consistent. Avoid words like "reboot" or "reset" for external comms — sounds aggressive.

Post-event followup items (for runbook / retro):
- Add a checklist to detect pre-warmup config drift.
- Add telemetry to show per-model cold-start penalty and expected warmup time.
- Run a tabletop next week to practice the sequence with product and CS.

Personal TODOs before weekend:
- Finalize 1-page bridge cheat-sheet and pin to channel (by EOD Fri) -> Arjun to review.
- Confirm CS blurb with Lina and Jess (CS lead).
- Create a short dashboard snapshot with p95 baseline and thresholds.

Rough timeline for 15-min cadences (example):
T+0: kickoff, initial observations, start phase 1
T+15: confirm phase 1 health -> continue to phase 2 or pause
T+30: data check (latency, errors), update to execs
T+45: more nodes, continue ramp, re-evaluate
T+60: if stable, enter monitoring/stabilization phase and prepare closure message

End notes (handy soundbites):
- "Phased restarts to avoid user-facing failures."
- "We're prioritizing stability over speed of recovery to keep errors low."
- "We will share an RCA once we have root cause confidence."

-- Nikita
